page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a woodcut-style diagram of a crescent-shaped segment and a set of concentric circles sit in the right half between paragraphs; a handwritten marginal word at top right edge and a handwritten stamp/annotation at bottom are not printed text; catchword "Sphæ-" at the foot right.

main_text.l: Circulares planæ aut una linea finiuntur, ut
circulus, aut pluribus ut ἀγωνια ἀχήματα, ex
quorum numero est à geometris dicta
σεφωνὴ, quam ὁμόκεντροι circuli delineant, & τὰ
γεγωνιωμένα ut μλωίσηοι, id est, figuræ quas segmen-
ta circulorum uelut sibi inuicem subtensa
& subiuncta atq; extremis coaptata terminis efformant.
quas non rectæ, sed circulares designant & deter-
Circulus & circus κύκλος, est figura in pla-
nicie, quam una includit linea circularis, quæ
linea ambitus dicitur, in cuius medio
punctum est, à quo omnes rectæ lineæ ad lineam ambitus eductæ,
inter se sunt æquales. Fit Circulus
lineæ rectæ uno puncto fixo, altero, cum tota linea circuma-
cto, donec in se reuoluatur. Punctum fixum cen-
trum circuli denotat. Alterum περιφέρεια deline-
at. His interclusa linea aream Circuli effingit.

page.notes: Diagram of crescent segments (unnumbered) and concentric circles not transcribed as text. Greek words transcribed as printed; the Greek forms ἀγωνια, ἀχήματα, σεφωνὴ, ὁμόκεντροι, γεγωνιωμένα, μλωίσηοι and κύκλος, περιφέρεια are approximate readings of the scan and may contain errors. Marginal handwritten word "orbiculare" at top right and handwritten annotations are not printed text.
